# Hub / engine / coordinator: current flow digest

<!-- LIVING digest: the current shape of this subsystem. Update it when you change the subsystem. -->

## What it is
The protocol-agnostic wiring that boots the daemon and connects everything else: process bootstrap (`cmd/ze/hub`), the `Engine` supervisor that starts/stops/reloads registered `ze.Subsystem`s in order, the `Coordinator` (a protocol-agnostic facade "created by the hub at startup" that lets any reactor register itself and defer work until every plugin has finished starting), and the managed/fleet client that lets an edge instance pull its config from a remote hub. Two different "subsystem" mechanisms coexist in the real code: `ze.Subsystem` + `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (used today only by L2TP and PPPoE) and the older Coordinator/`ReactorLifecycle` path (used by BGP, loaded as a config-path plugin through the plugin server, not through the Engine). This digest covers bootstrap and coordination; the per-message engine<->plugin wire protocol (5-stage handshake, EventBus, DirectBridge) is `ai/digests/plugin-transport.md`.

## Flow
1. **Entry and config-type probe.** `ze start` (`cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go:80` `cmdStart`) resolves blob storage, detects managed mode via `isManaged` (`cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go:231`), and calls `hub.Run` / `hub.RunWithManagedClient` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:101-109`) which both call `run()` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:111`). `run` reads the config bytes then `zeconfig.ProbeConfigType` (`internal/component/config/probe.go:21`) dispatches: `ConfigTypeBGP`/`ConfigTypeUnknown` -> `runYANGConfig` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:149`, defined `:203`), the path every real BGP deployment takes; `ConfigTypeHub` -> `runOrchestratorWithData` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:155`, defined `:1006`), the separate multi-process Orchestrator (step 13). BGP always wins when both a top-level `bgp{}` and `plugin{}` block are present (`internal/component/config/probe.go:61-63`), so the Orchestrator path is reached only by pure-plugin configs.
2. **Coordinator creation.** Inside `runYANGConfig`, after config parse/evolution/PKI setup, `coordinator := zePlugin.NewCoordinator(configTree)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:385`) builds the `*plugin.Coordinator` (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:36`), documented as "Created by the hub at startup" (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:26`). `coordinator.SetBootstrap(registry.BGPBootstrap{...})` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:392`) stashes config-load state (config path, CLI plugins, chaos flags, store, health/MRT callbacks) the BGP reactor factory reads back later, avoiding an import cycle between the hub and BGP.
3. **Server + Engine construction.** `pm := pluginmgr.NewManager()` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:405`, `internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:74`) implements `ze.PluginManager` (`pkg/ze/plugin.go:13`). `apiServer, _ := pluginserver.NewServer(serverConfig, coordinator)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:442`) hands the Coordinator to the plugin server as its `plugin.ReactorLifecycle` (`internal/component/plugin/server/server.go:156`). `apiServer.SetProcessSpawner(pm)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:447`) and `registry.SetEventBus(apiServer)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:454`) make the plugin server double as the `ze.EventBus` (`pkg/ze/eventbus.go:33`); there is no separate bus. `eng := engine.NewEngine(apiServer, configProvider, pm)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:503`, `internal/component/engine/engine.go:33`) builds the `ze.Engine` (`pkg/ze/engine.go:14`) supervisor.
4. **Subsystem registration (Engine-owned, protocol-agnostic).** Anything implementing `ze.Subsystem` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go:16`) registers with the Engine before `Start`: L2TP (`eng.RegisterSubsystem(l2tp.NewSubsystem(...))`, `cmd/ze/hub/main.go:518`, `internal/component/l2tp/subsystem.go:97`) and PPPoE (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:530`, `internal/component/l2tp/pppoe/subsystem.go:70`), each gated on its config block being present. `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (`internal/component/engine/engine.go:45`) rejects duplicate names and rejects any call after `Start`. BGP is deliberately NOT registered this way; see Invariants.
5. **Engine.Start: subsystems only, no plugin process yet.** `eng.Start(startCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:537`, `engine.go:66`) calls `e.plugins.StartAll(ctx, e.eventBus, e.config)` (`engine.go:75`), which for `pluginmgr.Manager` only marks itself started and stores ctx/eventBus/config (`internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:116`); no OS process is forked yet. It then starts every registered subsystem in registration order (`engine.go:80`), stopping already-started subsystems in reverse and calling `plugins.StopAll` on the first failure (`engine.go:82-88`).
6. **Plugin server start: the real fork happens here, after the Engine.** `apiServer.StartWithContext(startCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:543`, `internal/component/plugin/server/server.go:500`) launches `runPluginStartup` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go:130`) in a goroutine: five ordered phases, config-path plugins (bgp, iface, fib, ...) first, then explicit `plugin{external}` plugins, then auto-load by family/event/send-type, each phase calling `pm.SpawnMore` (`internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:139`) -> `spawnProcesses` (`internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:157`) and the 5-stage handshake (owned by `plugin-transport.md`). Because config-path plugins run in phase 1, BGP's reactor exists before anything that depends on it.
7. **BGP registers into the Coordinator during its own config callback.** The BGP plugin's `OnConfigure` handler (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go:108`) type-asserts the server's reactor to `registry.CoordinatorAccessor` (`internal/component/plugin/registry/interfaces.go:105`), builds the reactor via the registered factory, and calls `coord.SetReactor(bgpReactor.ReactorLifecycleAdapter())` (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go:153`, `Coordinator.SetReactor` `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:84`), the only reactor the Coordinator's named map holds in practice (`RegisterReactor`, `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:63`, is otherwise unused today). It starts the reactor's listeners immediately (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go:160`) but defers peer/session startup by registering `coord.OnPostStartup(func() { bgpReactor.StartPeers() })` (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go:168-169`, `Coordinator.OnPostStartup` `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:298`).
8. **Startup barrier -> deferred peer start.** When `runPluginStartup` finishes all five phases it calls `signalStartupComplete` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go:236`), which freezes the schema/subsystem/command registries for lock-free dispatch, fans a post-startup callback out to every plugin (`sendPostStartupToAll`, `internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go:265`), then calls `s.reactor.SignalPluginStartupComplete()` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go:255`). The Coordinator (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:283`) forwards to the BGP reactor and invokes its single stored `postStartup` closure (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:288-292`), the step-7 hook: peers start only once every plugin phase has finished, protocol-agnostically. Back in `main.go`, `apiServer.WaitForStartupComplete(startupCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:886`, `internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go:299`) blocks until this barrier fires before the `ze.ready.file` is written (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:898-901`).
9. **Managed client and run loop.** Only for blob-backed managed instances, `go managed.RunManagedClient(managedCtx, *managedClient)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:904`, `internal/component/managed/client.go:55`) starts the fleet client goroutine (step 11). `waitLoop` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:930`, defined `:981`) then blocks on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP or plugin-server exit (`waitForServerDone`, `cmd/ze/hub/main.go:974`).
10. **Reload: SIGHUP or managed push both drive `doReload`.** A SIGHUP is read by `handleSIGHUPReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:875`, defined `cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go:29`); a managed config push instead calls `reloadAfterCommit` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:606-619`) via the `OnCommit` hook wired in `wireManagedCommit` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed.go:15-20`). Both funnel into `doReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go:98`): load the config tree once, `s.ReloadConfig(ctx, newTree)` (plugin-server diff/apply, owned by `plugin-transport.md`), refresh the shared `zeconfig.Provider` root-by-root (`applyLoadedTreeToProvider`, `cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go:257`), then `eng.Reload(reloadCtx)` (`engine.go:125`) fans out to every registered `Subsystem.Reload` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go:29`). Any failure after the plugin-server step triggers `rollbackReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go:286`), replaying the prior tree through the plugin server and restoring the ConfigProvider snapshot.
11. **Managed client connection loop.** `RunManagedClient` (`internal/component/managed/client.go:55`) loops `runConnection` (`client.go:103`) with `Backoff` (`internal/component/managed/reconnect.go:14`, reset on successful auth, `client.go:155`): TLS-dial the hub, auth, `fetchAndProcess` (`client.go:203`) which calls `Handler.ValidateConfig` (`internal/component/managed/handler.go:46`) and, on success, the `ClientConfig.OnCommit` closure (the same `reloadAfterCommit` from step 10), then starts a `Heartbeat` (`internal/component/managed/heartbeat.go:18`, `NewHeartbeat` `:29`) and blocks in `notificationLoop` (`client.go:238`) handling hub-pushed `config-changed`/`ping` RPCs (`handleHubRequest`, `client.go:260`) until disconnect, heartbeat timeout, or context cancel.
12. **Shutdown: reverse of startup, plugin server first.** On signal, `main.go` calls `apiServer.Stop()` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:955`) before `eng.Stop(stopCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:956`, `engine.go:99`), which stops every subsystem in reverse registration order (`engine.go:109`) and finally `plugins.StopAll` (`engine.go:116`, `internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:293`), tearing down the shared `ProcessManager` and TLS acceptor.
13. **Alternate path: the multi-process Orchestrator.** `runOrchestratorWithData` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:1006`) parses via `hub.ParseHubConfig` (`internal/component/hub/config.go:47`), builds `hub.NewOrchestrator(cfg)` (`internal/component/hub/hub.go:53`), composing a `pluginserver.SubsystemManager` + `SchemaRegistry` + `Hub` router (`hub.go:58-76`) that forks each configured plugin as a separate `ze <name> --child` process instead of an in-process DirectBridge/goroutine plugin. `Orchestrator.Start` (`hub.go:86`) forks all, registers schemas, then `Freeze()`s both registries (`hub.go:105-106`). Its own SIGHUP handler calls `Orchestrator.Reload` (`internal/component/hub/reload.go:100`), which diffs plugin definitions (`diffPluginDefs`, `reload.go:22`), starts added/changed plugins before stopping removed ones, and rolls back on any start failure (`reload.go:177`). This path never touches `engine.Engine`, `ze.Subsystem`, or the Coordinator.

| `cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go` | `ze start` CLI: managed-mode detection, dispatch to `hub.Run`/`hub.RunWithManagedClient` |

## Invariants & gotchas
- **Two coexisting "subsystem" mechanisms.** `ze.Subsystem` + `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go:16`, `engine.go:45`) is used today only by L2TP and PPPoE. BGP (and iface/fib/etc.) load as config-path plugins through the plugin server and register into the Coordinator instead (step 7); despite `plan/learned/425-arch-0-system-boundaries.md` saying "the BGP daemon is a subsystem," it does not implement `ze.Subsystem` or call `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` in the current code.
- **Engine.Start finishes before any plugin process exists.** `Manager.StartAll` (called from `engine.go:75`) is a Phase-1 no-op (`internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go:116`); the real fork happens later and separately via `apiServer.StartWithContext` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:543`). L2TP/PPPoE are fully started before BGP even begins its 5-stage handshake.
- **`Coordinator.postStartup` is a single closure, not a list** (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:32`). Only BGP calls `OnPostStartup` today (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go:168`); a second protocol reactor calling it would silently overwrite BGP's deferred-peer-start hook. `RegisterReactor`'s named-reactor map (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go:63`) is likewise unused beyond the single `"bgp"` entry set by `SetReactor`.
- **`ConfigTypeBGP` always beats `ConfigTypeHub`** when both a `bgp{}` and `plugin{}` block are top-level (`internal/component/config/probe.go:61-63`), so the `internal/component/hub` Orchestrator is reached only by pure-plugin configs; it has its own integration test (`test/hub/startup_test.go`) but is effectively unreachable for any real BGP daemon started via `ze start`.
- **Docs describe an aspirational, not-yet-collapsed design.** `docs/architecture/hub-architecture.md` is explicitly headed "Design aspiration (partially implemented)"; `docs/architecture/subsystem-wiring.md` and `docs/architecture/plugin-manager-wiring.md` both describe an intermediate "BGPSubsystem wraps Server" shape that the live code does not have (`Server`/`apiServer` is created directly in `cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, before any reactor exists). Both docs point back at `cmd/ze/hub/main.go` as authoritative; trust the code over the diagrams.
- **The fleet hub server side is unwired.** `internal/component/managed` is the client only. Its hub-side counterpart, `ManagedConfigService` (`internal/component/plugin/server/managed.go:29`), implements `HandleConfigFetch`/`BuildConfigChanged` and is exercised only by its own unit tests; nothing in production code constructs it or wires it into the plugin server's TLS acceptor/dispatcher, so no `ze` instance can currently serve config to a managed client despite the client side being fully wired into `cmd/ze/hub/main.go`.
- **Managed pushes and SIGHUP share one commit path.** `wireManagedCommit`'s `OnCommit` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed.go:16-20`) writes a candidate version then calls the exact same `reloadAfterCommit` closure SIGHUP/API/SSH commits use (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go:606-619`), so a managed push gets the same validate/diff/apply/rollback guarantees as any other commit.
- **Reload rollback covers the plugin server and ConfigProvider, not subsystems individually.** `rollbackReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go:286`) replays the prior tree through `s.ReloadConfig` and restores the ConfigProvider snapshot, then calls `eng.Reload` again with the restored provider; it does not separately undo whatever partial state a subsystem's own `Reload` mutated before the failure.
- **Orchestrator reload starts new/changed plugins before stopping old ones** (`internal/component/hub/reload.go:186-214`), the same "never leave nothing running" principle as `Engine.Start`'s failure rollback, but implemented independently (the Orchestrator never calls into `engine.Engine`).
